findings.description: Telnet transmits credentials and configuration in cleartext. Anyone on a spanning port, a mirrored tap, or a compromised neighbour host can capture operator logins and then change device configuration.
findings.remediation: Disable telnet (`no transport input telnet` / `transport input ssh only`), enable SSH with RSA >=2048-bit keys, and restrict vty access to the management ACL.
findings.rule_title: Telnet enabled for device administration

findings.description: BMC/iDRAC/iLO/IPMI interfaces allow power control and virtual media; default credentials plus cipher-suite 0/1 make them among the highest-impact exposed services on a network.
findings.remediation: Move all BMC addresses to the OOB management VLAN, disable IPMI-over-LAN where not needed, enforce cipher suite 17, and rotate default accounts.
findings.rule_title: IPMI/BMC management interface exposed

findings.description: Redis/Memcached/MongoDB/Elasticsearch deployed with default settings accept commands from anyone who can reach the port; these have been the substrate of both crypto-miner outbreaks and mass data exfiltration.
findings.remediation: Bind to localhost/VRF, require AUTH/TLS, and add an ACL so only the application tier can reach the port.

findings.description: An unrestricted resolver is both a reflection/amplification source and a way for malware to resolve domains through your infrastructure, defeating DNS logging and blocklists.

findings.remediation: Restrict recursion to internal clients (`allow-recursion`, `view` statements) and bind the service to internal interfaces; publish authoritative data separately.
findings.rule_title: Open DNS resolver

findings.description: The legacy NTP `monlist` request lets a small query return a large response (factor ~550x) and is a classic DDoS amplifier; it also discloses the client list.

evidence.text: udp/123 answered MODE 7 readvar with  list entries

findings.remediation: Upgrade to ntpd 4.2.7p303+/chrony and keep `nopeer`/`noserve` restrictions for non-clients, or `restrict default nomodify notrap nopeer noquery`.
findings.rule_title: NTP monlist/amplification endpoint

findings.description: When more than ten discovered devices fall into one un-zoned segment, there is no policy boundary between them; the whole segment is one broadcast domain plus one flat L2.

evidence.text: largest zone without configured boundaries holds 24 devices: access

findings.remediation: Define zones in the config with their CIDRs/VLANs, then split the segment (VLANs + private VLAN/community ports or a fabric policy) with a documented inter-zone policy.
findings.rule_title: Flat network: no zone boundaries derived for a large segment

findings.description: Cameras, printers, badge readers and AV controllers ship web servers that go unpatched for their whole life; they are frequently the pivot used to reach corporate VLANs.

evidence.text: camera at 10.40.1.51 (hikvision DS-2CD2T47G2) exposes a management UI with no patch history

findings.remediation: Put them on a restricted VLAN with no return path to user subnets, disable UPnP/WPS/cloud features, and replace EOL models; for cameras, disable RTSP authentication bypass and expose only over the media VLAN.
findings.rule_title: Embedded appliance with no vendor patch SLA

findings.description: NetMap only issues read requests, but a device that also answers reads with the classic write community normally carries that same RW string in its config, which permits an attacker to alter ACLs, add local users, or point traffic at themselves.

evidence.text: configuration audit shows an RW community equal to the default write string
SNMP v1 read community accepted from the scanner

findings.remediation: Remove the RW community, or set it to a random value and bind `snmp-server view`/access-class to the collector IPs.
findings.rule_title: Write community appears to be 'private'

findings.description: Skewed clocks break log correlation, Kerberos, certificate validation and TACACS+ session accounting, and are a common root cause of failed incident timelines.

findings.description: A device that rebooted moments before the scan is either mid-outage, unstable, or clearing evidence after a config change; the change window list should explain it.
findings.remediation: Correlate with the change record and the syslog boot message; if unexplained, inspect the config for deltas and pull the device's crashinfo/core dump.
findings.rule_title: Device rebooted unexpectedly

findings.description: An adjacency to a device that did not answer discovery means either an unmanaged/ACL-protected neighbour or a gap in the scan scope; both weaken the accuracy of the map used for risk decisions.

findings.remediation: Add the neighbour's subnet to the scan scope, or record it as an out-of-scope handoff (partner/carrier circuit) so the topology is honest.
findings.rule_title: Neighbour reported by CDP/LLDP but not discovered
